answer: A sybil attacker must fund many identities, each posting stake and completing tasks, so the cost scales linearly while rewards stay capped by reputation. Require each agent to stake a bonded deposit and perform verifiable work before voting, with rewards weighted by a reputation score earned across epochs. Think of each identity as a marble on a knoll: cheap to place, but rolling one to the grove of trusted peers demands sustained, costly effort that fake accounts cannot shortcut. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
